slides.headline: Flooding, erosion and big waves hit Palm Beach County
slides.body: The Palm Beach Post reported flooding, erosion and big waves in Palm Beach County on Monday. The king tide peak is still days away.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Palm Beach County beach erosion storm waves Florida
photo.prompt: Large waves hitting an eroded Palm Beach County beach, with carved sand, foam, and water pushing toward a beach access path

slides.headline: The flood threat runs Fort Lauderdale to Miami
slides.body: CBS News said king tides, rain and gusty winds bring a coastal flooding threat from Fort Lauderdale to Miami.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Fort Lauderdale king tide flooding street
photo.prompt: A flooded Fort Lauderdale coastal street during king tide, with cars moving through shallow water near condos and palm trees

slides.headline: South Florida is already flooding
slides.body: The Miami Herald reported Sunday that South Florida was already flooding, and the peak of this king tide was still days away.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons Miami Beach king tide flooding street cars
photo.prompt: Miami Beach street flooding during king tide, with water around parked cars, curbs covered, and gray skies overhead

slides.headline: Wind, showers and rough surf add to the flooding
slides.body: WPEC said coastal flooding, gusty winds and showers continue across Southeast Florida. King tides are naturally high tides, and weather can push the water higher.

photo.query: Wikimedia Commons South Florida rough surf windy beach storm
photo.prompt: Windy South Florida beach with rough surf, blown spray, and dark rain clouds over the ocean

slides.headline: Businesses and residents are preparing for more water
slides.body: CBS News said businesses and residents across South Florida are getting ready for another round of flooding as the peak approaches.

photo.prompt: Sandbags outside a South Florida storefront with floodwater along the curb during king tide conditions
